```{r}
#library(rentrez)

# Function to retrieve 16S sequences for a given species
retrieve_16S_sequences <- function(species_name) {
  query <- paste0(species_name, "[Organism] AND 16S[All Fields] AND (33175[BioProject] OR 33317[BioProject])")
  search_results <- entrez_search(db = "nuccore", term = query, retmax = 10)
  
  if (length(search_results$ids) == 0) {
    message("No results found for: ", species_name)
    return(data.frame(Species = species_name, Sequence = NA))
  } else {
    message("Found IDs for ", species_name, ": ", paste(search_results$ids, collapse = ", "))
    sequence_data <- entrez_fetch(db = "nuccore", id = search_results$ids, rettype = "fasta")
    return(data.frame(Species = species_name, Sequence = sequence_data, ID = search_results$ids))
  }
}

# Retrieve sequences for each species in the species_list
sequences_list <- lapply(species_list, retrieve_16S_sequences)

##For species with multiple 'hits', every hit is a concatenation of all hits. We must correct this before proceeding. 
# Function to split concatenated sequences into individual entries
split_concatenated_sequences <- function(species_entry) {
  # Ensure the Sequence column is a character vector
  species_entry$Sequence <- as.character(species_entry$Sequence)
  
  sequences <- unlist(strsplit(species_entry$Sequence, split = "\n\n"))
  unique_sequences <- unique(sequences)
  
  return(data.frame(Species = rep(species_entry$Species[1], length(unique_sequences)), 
                    Sequence = unique_sequences, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}

# Apply the function to all entries in sequences_list
cleaned_sequences_list <- lapply(sequences_list, split_concatenated_sequences)

# Retain only the first hit for each species
cleaned_sequences_list <- lapply(cleaned_sequences_list, function(species_entry) {
  if (nrow(species_entry) > 1) {
    return(species_entry[1, , drop = FALSE])
  } else {
    return(species_entry)
  }
})

# Combine the results into a single data frame
cleaned_sequences_df_new <- do.call(rbind, cleaned_sequences_list)


```

```{r}
##Let's now perform a multiple sequence alignment
library(ape)
library(msa)
library(seqinr)
library(ggtree)
library(phangorn)

# Function to clean and validate sequences
clean_sequences <- function(sequence) {
  sequence <- gsub("[^AGCTagct]", "", sequence) # Remove non-DNA characters
  return(sequence)
}

# Apply the cleaning function to the Sequence column
cleaned_sequences_df_new$Sequence <- sapply(cleaned_sequences_df_new$Sequence, clean_sequences)

# Remove any rows with empty sequences
cleaned_sequences_df_new <- cleaned_sequences_df_new[cleaned_sequences_df_new$Sequence != "", ]

# Correct FASTA entry creation function
create_fasta_entry <- function(row) {
  header <- paste0(">", row["Species"])
  sequence <- row["Sequence"]
  return(paste(header, sequence, sep = "\n"))
}

# Convert data frame to FASTA format
fasta_entries <- apply(cleaned_sequences_df_new, 1, create_fasta_entry)

# Write the FASTA entries to a file
fasta_file <- "/Users/brett/Documents/sequences_corrected.fasta"
writeLines(fasta_entries, con = fasta_file)

# Read the sequences from the FASTA file
sequences <- readDNAStringSet(fasta_file, format = "fasta")

# Verify the sequences before alignment
print(sequences)

# Perform multiple sequence alignment
alignment <- msaMuscle(inputSeqs = sequences, 
                        cluster = "upgma", 
                        maxiters = 12, 
                        substitutionMatrix = "default",
                        type = "default", 
                        order = "aligned",
                        verbose = TRUE)
  #msa(sequences, method = "ClustalW")

# Convert alignment to a phyDat object
alignment_phyDat <- as.phyDat(alignment)

# Construct the phylogenetic tree using neighbor-joining method
distance_matrix <- dist.ml(alignment_phyDat)
phylo_tree <- nj(distance_matrix)

# Perform bootstrapping
bootstrap_replicates <- 1000  # Number of bootstrap replicates

# Function to generate a tree from bootstrap sample
bootstrap_trees <- bootstrap.phyDat(alignment_phyDat, FUN = function(x) {
  dist_matrix <- dist.ml(x)
  nj(dist_matrix)
}, bs = bootstrap_replicates)

# Compute the bootstrap values
bootstrap_values <- prop.clades(phylo_tree, bootstrap_trees)


# Save the tree in Newick format
tree_file <- "/Users/brett/Documents/phylo_tree.nwk"
write.tree(phylo_tree, file = tree_file)

tree.1 <- ggtree(phylo_tree, layout="fan", ignore.negative.edge=TRUE)

tree.2 <- ggtree(phylo_tree, layout="equal_angle", ignore.negative.edge=TRUE)

```

```{r}
# Create new metadata object
metadata_df_family <- data.frame(Species = phylo_tree$tip.label, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(taxonomy_df, by = "Species") %>%
  left_join(final_df.3, by = "Species") %>%
  dplyr::select(Species, Family, everything()) %>%
  mutate(
    Family = gsub("\\[|\\]", "", Family),
    Family = ifelse(Family == "" | is.na(Family), "Unknown", Family)
  )

# Assign Family names as rownames
rownames(metadata_df_family) <- metadata_df_family$Species
metadata_df_family <- metadata_df_family[phylo_tree$tip.label, ]

# Define family color palette (same as stacked barplot)
custom_family_colors <- c(
  "Carnobacteriaceae"   = "#fcfdbf",
  "Lactobacillaceae"    = "#febb81",
  "Staphylococcaceae"   = "#f8765c",
  "Dermabacteraceae"    = "#d3436e",
  "Nocardiopsaceae"     = "#982d80",
  "Bacillaceae"         = "#5f187f",
  "Micrococcaceae"      = "#221150",
  "<5% abund."          = "#000004"
)

# Replace low abundance families with "<5% abund." (ensure consistent handling)
metadata_df_family <- metadata_df_family %>%
  mutate(Family = ifelse(!Family %in% names(custom_family_colors)[custom_family_colors != "#000004"], "<5% abund.", Family))

# Generate tree plot with tips colored by Family
tree_family <- ggtree(phylo_tree, layout = "equal_angle", 
                      aes(color = Family), ignore.negative.edge = TRUE, size = 0.5) %<+% metadata_df_family +
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_family_colors) +
  theme(legend.position = 'none')

# Save the figure
ggsave("phylogenetic_tree_by_family.png", tree_family, width = 4, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 900)

```
